text:
nora: Hey team, noticed ~6 GPU nodes failing to reach model-registry.internal since ~07:05 UTC, some get NX, some get the old split-horizon IP. Rolling jobs are hitting wrong backends.
liam: which AZs?
nora: a and c. b looks fine. All repro from pods that use the node-local stub (10.100.0.53).
ajay: can you paste dig +trace?
maria: saw a pattern — answers differ depending on whether the node forwarded to the edge forwarder or directly to the recursive. TTLs also vary.
nora: paste below:
```
; node-1 (AZ-a)
$ dig +short model-registry.internal @10.100.0.53
10.200.11.5
; node-3 (AZ-c)
$ dig +short model-registry.internal @10.100.0.53
SERVFAIL
; dig @10.200.0.2 (edge-forwarder)
$ dig +short model-registry.internal @10.200.0.2
10.200.11.5
```
liam: hmmm SERVFAIL from node-local means stub probably returned error from its cache or upstream. Any recent config changes?
ajay: earlier today we rolled a change that increased ndots to 2 in DHCP for pods and switched node-local-dns to prefer systemd-resolved when available.
maria: that change may have changed search path behavior — some queries might be sent as FQDN vs relative which can hit split-horizon differently.
sre-oncall: seeing a spike in negative caching entries TTL on the forwarder metrics (negative_cache_count). Could be stale NX/servfail cached and propagated back to node-local.
nora: confirmed negative_cache_count spiked around 07:03.
liam: quick mitigation options?
ajay: 1) flush caches on the edge forwarders (sudo systemctl restart bind9 on forwarders) 2) restart node-local-dns on affected nodes 3) optionally add a short /etc/hosts entry as hotfix for model-registry.internal -> 10.200.11.5 on the few nodes running critical pods.
maria: we tried restart node-local-dns on one node and it resolved immediately.
sre-oncall: flushing edge forwarder cache fixed 4 more nodes. But 2 nodes still sporadically return SERVFAIL.
liam: what about conntrack / NAT path differences? could egress NAT mapping cause queries to hit different upstream clusters with different split-horizon views?
ajay: good call — those 2 nodes are behind a different NAT gateway after an autoscale. The NAT has an old route to an on-prem recursive that doesn't have the internal zone.
nora: so combination: ndots/search path change -> some queries sent as relative -> forwarded to different upstreams depending on NAT path -> hit upstream without internal zone -> NX/SERVFAIL -> negative cached -> node-local returns SERVFAIL.
maria: TL;DR: incoherent upstream views + caching + stub config change.
sre-oncall: actions taken: flushed forwarder caches in AZ-a/c, restarted node-local-dns on affected nodes, added temporary hosts entries on 2 remaining nodes, removed the problematic NAT route (rollback) to force consistent egress.
liam: can we add a healthcheck for model-registry internal resolution at node-provisioner level? if nodes get an unexpected answer, alert before scheduling work.
ajay: yes, I'll add a probe in node bootstrap that runs `dig +short model-registry.internal @10.100.0.53` and fails if it returns NX/SERVFAIL or the wrong IP.
maria: long-term fix: pin stub behavior (always send FQDNs for internal domains), standardize upstream forwarders per region, and avoid short-lived NAT route divergence during autoscale. Also lower negative caching TTLs for internal zones.
nora: thanks all. I pushed hosts temp fix to the 2 nodes, will watch. Planning to revert ndots/search tweak until we get deterministic behavior.
sre-oncall: monitoring: added a dashboard metric for downstream failed lookups and an alert if failed lookups > 5% over 5m in any AZ.
dns-bot: note: config-change detected earlier today: dhcpd: added "option domain-search" change, rollout id=deploy-20260315-ndots-bump
liam: please post a short postmortem if this recurs. For now, looks mitigated for most clusters. :thumbsup:
